question: What primary event defines the initiation of an infection in the human body?

options.B: Pathogen invasion, multiplication, and tissue reaction
options.D: Nutrient depletion in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: An infection officially begins when a pathogen invades body tissues, multiplies, and triggers a local or systemic reaction. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is understanding the infection process vital for student nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene
options.B: To implement effective preventive strategies and break transmission cycles
options.C: To diagnose all infectious diseases without laboratory testing
options.D: To replace physicians in prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Recognizing the dynamics of infection allows nurses to implement effective preventive strategies, breaking the cycle of disease transmission in healthcare and community settings. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of the six links in the chain of infection?

options.A: Host, Reservoir, Portal of Entry, Pathogen, Exit, Transmission
options.B: Infectious Agent, Reservoir, Portal of Exit, Mode of Transmission, Portal of Entry, Susceptible Host
options.C: Vector, Pathogen, Transmission, Host, Reservoir, Exit
options.D: Reservoir, Susceptible Host, Agent, Entry, Exit, Transmission

explanation: The chain consists of the infectious agent, reservoir, portal of exit, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host in continuous sequence. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary significance of identifying the chain of infection in nursing practice?

options.A: It allows nurses to break any single link to stop the infection process.
options.B: It proves that all infections originate from animal reservoirs.
options.C: It determines the exact financial cost of hospital stays.
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient vital sign monitoring.

explanation: Breaking any single link in the chain stops the infection process, forming the basis of all infection control precautions. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why are viruses classified as obligate intracellular parasites?

options.A: They can survive independently on dry surfaces indefinitely.
options.B: They require a living host cell to replicate.
options.C: They are easily treated with standard antibacterial soaps.
options.D: They contain complex peptidoglycan cell walls.

explanation: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites because they must invade living host cells to reproduce and multiply. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which microorganism type is primarily responsible for causing malaria in endemic regions like Nigeria?
explanation: Plasmodium species, which cause malaria, belong to the category of parasites that live inside a host organism. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which stage of clinical infection is characterized by vague, non-specific symptoms and high contagiousness?
explanation: The prodromal stage features non-specific symptoms like fatigue and malaise, and patients are often highly contagious because they feel relatively normal. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h4)

question: What defines the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The time between pathogen entry and the appearance of the first symptoms
options.B: The period when specific disease signs are most severe
options.C: The phase of complete recovery and tissue repair
options.D: The time when non-specific fatigue first appears

explanation: The incubation period is the exact interval between when the pathogen invades the host and when the first signs and symptoms manifest. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which component of the immune system is primarily responsible for humoral immunity by producing antibodies?
explanation: B cells are responsible for humoral immunity through the production of specific antibodies against circulating antigens. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the inflammatory response as a nonspecific defense mechanism?

options.A: To synthesize permanent antibodies against viral strains
options.B: To deliver fluid, blood products, and nutrients to neutralize pathogens and promote healing
options.C: To permanently lower the body temperature to prevent microbial replication
options.D: To halt all blood circulation near the site of injury

explanation: Inflammation is a vascular and cellular reaction that brings protective elements to injured tissues to neutralize pathogens and facilitate tissue repair. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which blood test result is commonly associated with an active bacterial infection during a Complete Blood Count (CBC)?
explanation: Bacterial infections typically trigger leukocytosis, which is an elevated white blood cell count as the body fights off the pathogen. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of performing microbiological culture and sensitivity testing?

options.A: To measure the patient's red blood cell volume
options.B: To identify the specific causative pathogen and effective antimicrobial medications
options.C: To assess the patient's long-term nutritional status
options.D: To determine the exact stage of the incubation period

explanation: Culture and sensitivity tests identify the exact microorganism causing the infection and determine which antibiotics will successfully treat it. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is considered the single most effective nursing measure for preventing healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Wearing sterile gowns during all patient interactions
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Isolating every admitted patient in a negative-pressure room

explanation: Hand hygiene is universally recognized as the single most effective intervention to stop the transmission of infectious agents in healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is patient education on completing a full course of prescribed antibiotics critically important?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital readmissions
options.B: To prevent the development of antimicrobial resistance
options.C: To ensure immediate normalization of white blood cell counts
options.D: To eliminate the need for standard hand hygiene practices

explanation: Completing the full course of antibiotics ensures all pathogens are eradicated, preventing surviving bacteria from developing antimicrobial resistance. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h7)

question: What serious condition occurs when pathogens enter the bloodstream and trigger a severe, life-threatening systemic inflammatory response?
explanation: Sepsis occurs when bloodstream infections trigger a massive systemic inflammatory response that can lead to organ failure and shock. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h8)

question: Which of the following is a potential long-term complication of untreated or recurrent streptococcal infections?
explanation: Untreated streptococcal infections, such as strep throat, can lead to serious long-term complications like rheumatic heart disease. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T3#GNS123_U4_T3_h8)
